title: Richard Jones, Canal Street Boogie and the Mercury job that never came
summary: Levy remembers Richard Jones, who tried to help him join ASCAP and was about to become A&R man for Mercury when he died.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

And you know, let me tell you, excuse me, I could, I don't know if it was the day before or the week before he called me up. He said, Charlie, get your tunes together. We're all set. right around the corner from me.

Yeah, yeah, sure. And he said, we're on the South Street. He says, we're little, but we're going to go. And I just felt so enthused. I was so happy. And then about a week later, he had an heart attack and died. So, it kind of upset me because we have a, we've got a boogie-woogie called Canal Street Boogie, Richard Jones and I wrote. And, you know, I thought, I said, well, I was feeling good. And then I, when I heard about him dying, I felt so very bad. He was such a, he always liked me. He knew that I knew so much more music than he did. See, he didn't know very much music. Did you know him in New Orleans? Slightly. But when he first came up here, then, he saw me playing violin with Whitley's band. And he told me who he was. He was from New Orleans. He had, what did he have, a cripple leg, I think? Yeah, he's stiff-legged. He got shot from the knee. Oh, yeah. And, and, he always liked me.
He was always trying to do something.
Always, yeah, yeah. He wanted to put me in,
he told me, I'll put you in that, ASCAP. Yeah. Yeah. I'd be in there with you. Yeah. And you don't have to worry. He says, I'll get you in there for $15. And I ain't done enough to join.
Yeah. Well, that's what he wanted to do with, we had this Canal Street Boogie and I had some other tunes.
All the Canal Streets are, the New Orleans Canal Street, aren't they? Yeah. We have the Canal Street in Chicago. Yeah. Yeah. It's Canal Street in New Orleans.

It all depends on you. That was the first record I would make. Yeah. With Richard. With Richard. I sang.
Yeah. That was OK. OK, that's right. He was a man for OK.
